notes.title: Disastr_Blastr now just $1.99 USD!
notes.notes:
Happy New Year Everyone! 

[b]It has been an amazing year for Disastr_Blastr![/b] After 1 year on Steam this game has close to 24k activations, and the Soundtrack_to_Disastr has been downloaded over 6k times! This is more than I ever dreamed possible when I started building a simple block-based shooter for the X360 back in 2013. I am totally overwhelmed guys!!! Thanks to every one of you for making my first year as a Steam developer truly unforgettable. 

[b]Huge thanks once again to everyone who played Disastr_Blastr,[/b] and especially those of you who supported this project by writing a Steam review, posting on social media, and by talking about it with your gaming friends. You guys are seriously awesome, so thanks! 

[b]After careful consideration, I feel the time is right to permanently lower the Steam price of Disastr_Blastr from $4.99 USD to just $1.99 USD.[/b] I hope this will open the door to even more players discovering this special little game. :) 

Have an awesome 2018 guys! Talk to you again soon!  


-Joel
Dog Theory Games

notes.title: Disastr_Blastr 1_Year_Blastiversary Event Begins!
notes.notes:
[b]The Disastr_Blastr 1 Year Blastiversary event is upon us![/b]

November 21 marks one year of abstract minimalist cubic destruction on Steam, and to honor this momentous occasion I have set up a groovy little sale that will run for the next 2 weeks (November 6-20). 

I thought about doing something a bit more fun like printing some signature Disastr_Blastr coffee mugs and giving them away... but finally decided against it, just because I suspect there may not be all that much interest from players. If you really, really want a signature coffee mug signed by the developer, send me a private message and we can work something out. I think they are like $14 each on Vistaprint. :)

In the meantime, please mention this epic Blastiversary event to your PC gaming friends! The game and soundtrack are each just $1, and I (your humble game designer) would be especially grateful to anyone willing to give the game a play and post a review on Steam. :)

Happy birthday to Disastr_Blastr, and to all you fearless block jockeys out there, happy blasting!!!!!!

-Joel
Dog Theory Games

-Joel

notes.title: Welcome Players!
notes.notes:
Hi guys! Welcome to the Disastr_Blastr community! 

I have been noticing a big spike in Steam activations over the last few weeks, and I just want to personally thank you guys for checking out Disastr_Blastr. This is my first released title as an indie designer, and it really means a lot to see so many Steam players giving it a play, so thank you!!!

If you guys have the time, [b]please take a minute to post a review here on Steam![/b] It doesn't have to be 20 pages on why Disastr_Blastr is awesome (unless you really want to write that!), just a sentence or two with your impressions on the game would be wonderful. 

If you look around the Steam store page you will see there are actually something like 28 reviews, almost all of them positive, however... [b]the only reviews that actually contribute to a game's official review score on Steam are the ones written by players like you guys[/b]. Every single review really helps, and I promise to personally respond to each and every one! Thank you guys so much for your support, I really appreciate it. :)

Also! You should Like the official Disastr_Blastr Facebook page: 
[url=https://www.facebook.com/disastrblastr/] Disastr_Blastr on Facebook	[/url]

I hope you guys enjoy the game! Best of luck and happy blasting!!!


-Joel Christiansen
Game Artist/Designer at Dog Theory
www.dogtheorygames.com

notes.title: Disastr_Blastr Indie Film in Production...
notes.notes:
Whats up Steam friends!

As you guys might know, [b]there is a Disastr_Blastr independent film currently in the works![/b] It is a big project, and honestly between school, normal life, and various other creative pursuits it has been tricky finding time to work on it. Today I shelved everything else for a few hours and captured some gameplay from old versions of Disastr_Blastr starting at the very beginning (January 2013). Got about 30 to 40 minutes of video so far, just from the first few months of a 4-year dev cycle!
 
[b]Nicholas Campbell[/b] and his crew have been busy digitizing all the home video footage from the last several years. This essentially means sitting around watching me talk to a camera for 19 hours, a fate I wouldn't really wish on anyone but... such is the road to indie film glory.  :)
 
Per usual I have no real idea how long this project will take. I think finishing by Summer 2017 is a halfway reasonable goal, but you know how these things go. :) 
 
Take care guys, talk to you again soon!
-Joel

notes.title: Dog_Theory at PAX South!
notes.notes:
Got some great news guys! I just received word that I will be joining a distinguished panel of experts at [b]PAX South[/b] in January 2017!

The panel is called: [b]"Embracing The Chaos Emeralds: Understanding Your Nerd Power"[/b], and will explore the psychology of feeling like you don't fit in, the negative effects of not accepting who you are, and the path to embracing, loving, and accepting your geek fortitude/fandom. 

This is a topic I am extremely passionate about, and I am very honored to be discussing the virtues of nerdhood alongside some very knowledgeable and respected speakers. :) Hope to see some of you guys there! 

Please feel free to find me anywhere at PAX and let me know how you are liking Disastr_Blastr! I might even have a limited edition custom Disastr_Blastr sticker for you (got a few left from the game release party).... Take care and keep it real guys! #indieforlife #destroyallcubes

~Joel

notes.title: Gameplay Videos!
notes.notes:
Just one week until launch day! Hope you guys are ready! 

Please take a second to check out all the wonderful Disastr_Blastr gameplay videos put together by esteemed members of the YouTube community. It is an honor to see so many talented creators taking a crack at this game! And of course if you like what you see, please consider subscribing to these channels. These great guys and gals are indies in their own right, and put a lot of work into their content just like us humble game designers. :D

So ok, if you guys have seen the video by KevGuuey, he makes some pretty strong points about the intensity of the player death VFX. In recognition of this video I have started calling it the "Green Flash of Doom", which shall forever henceforth be its name... But ok seriously, upon giving it some thought I agree with the point that this effect is a little over the top and could be disturbing to some players, so—I have made a small change to where the GFoD no longer flickers in strobe-light fashion, it just goes green for an instant and then smoothly fades away. I hope you all find this to be an improvement! 

That's all I got for you guys right now. Stay tuned for more epic videos! And if you feel like it go ahead and post your own vid or screenshots! Take care everyone! 

-Joel
